$comment: The last commit covered by a stage audit whose findings are written into docs/JOURNAL.md.
The stage audit used to be periodic — run at the end of a stage, against the tree. That was
right for the 43-finding audit, which caught things that had sat for weeks. It is the wrong
shape for what the evidence now says produces most defects: this project's own record shows
them arriving INSIDE the proofs and instruments written an hour earlier to close the previous
defect. The separator gap that gave the guard its only false negative, the crash the
history-reach fix introduced, the verdict state that printed in no output, and two wrong
entries in a licence notice were all fix-induced.
So the audit is scoped to a range rather than a moment. `npm run audit:scope` reports
watermark..HEAD, and CLAUDE.md's checklist is applied to that range instead of to the tree.
This file advances ONLY in the commit that writes the findings, and check:docs enforces that
by requiring this sha to appear in docs/JOURNAL.md — the same shape as a FEATURES.md row that
turns the check red when it is claimed without evidence.
ORIGIN, CORRECTED 2026-08-18. It first read 710cd94 with 'batches 1-7, each audited at close'.
That was ASSERTED from the presence of batch COMPLETION records, not established from audit
records, and it is wrong: docs/JOURNAL.md marks Batch 7 'PART DONE'. A batch that never closed
was never audited at close, and Batch 7 is 31 commits.
The origin is now a969ae4 — 'Record Batch 6' — the last commit of the last batch that closed.
Batches 1 to 6 each carry a journal entry with findings; 3 and 6 carry explicit stage-audit
sections. That is a defensible lower bound. 710cd94 was not.
The consequence is immediate and correct: the gate reports an audit owed for Batch 7 from the
day the mechanism exists, rather than starting green on a claim nobody checked.
This is the failure the origin was always going to have. It is the one value in this mechanism
nobody revisits, so an assumed origin makes every later range inherit the gap in silence —
which is precisely what the watermark exists to prevent. It survived one question.
audited: Batches 1-6; Batch 7 in four ranges (a969ae4..2aaa8f7, ..63242af, ..bcdf209, ..513b061), findings R1-1, R2-1, R3-1; 513b061..caa59d0 folded into the security-substrate amendment; caa59d0..d9f01b0 — identity, DocumentService and the advisory register — findings R-1 to R-8, both open ones since closed in f1737be and fe2274b; and d9f01b0..8f097e3 — the lane, the version counter and the command declaration — findings S-1 (the compile-fail harness accepts any error as a rejection, so a case can pass for a reason it does not claim) and S-2 (the engine seam's both-shapes claim has no control until a byte-image fixture exists); and 8f097e3..b315e2c — the compile-fail harness hardening, the guard's NUL widening and the engine seam — findings T-1 (a reachability verdict's path glob has a positive control and its SYMBOL has none, so a misspelt symbol leaves the verdict green forever; measured) and T-2 (the adapter's retention test asserts equal LENGTH where equal bytes were available and hold). Both since closed — T-2 by comparing the bytes, T-1 by requiring every symbol to be derived, witnessed, or printed as unverifiable against a separate count; and b315e2c..77d4c2c — the witness rule, rotatePages and the command log — findings U-1 (the file guard scans C0 plus 0x7f byte-wise and cannot see the Trojan Source class at all, CVE-2021-42574; verified absent from all 183 tracked text files with a positive control, so a gap rather than a defect) and U-2 (the modified-proofs column reports NET range change, so a proof loosened in one commit and re-tightened in another shows zero deletions; measured, and open with the fix named) — both since closed; and 77d4c2c..d61d995 — C's inverse, the capability narrowing and the log moving onto the record — findings V-1 (the append-only control in auditScope.proof.mjs has never tested anything: its fixture is ADDED in the range so it never reaches the modified-proofs column, and `appended === undefined ||` makes not-found pass) and V-2 (the report a human reads has no test at all — the proof exercises auditScope, never scope.mjs, so deleting the hidden-deletions line passes every case). Both since closed; and d61d995..f144768 — section 9's failure type, the composition point and the first IPC handler — findings W-1 (this report's own proof classifier matched *.proof.mjs and proofs/ only, so every *.test.ts was invisible to both columns: a range that added 254 lines of test carrying its strongest control reported 'proofs ADDED: none'), W-2 (the contract compile-fail proof holds its fixtures as STRINGS, so typecheck cannot see them; it drifted twice in one range, once leaving main red for three pushes), W-3 (the reachability walk reads tracked files only, so a new source file is invisible to every verdict until it is staged — not a defect, an unwritten consequence) and W-4 (a comment in a scanned file is scanned text, second occurrence). All four closed in the recording commit; W-2 with a conditional pre-commit gate rather than a rule; and f144768..81b9b2b — the lockfile repair, the toolchain pin, the write-target correction and the first CI runs in two days — findings G-1 (HEAD did not typecheck and the file that failed was a control; proof:toolchain, lint and test were run before committing and typecheck was not), G-2 (NOTICE was under-declaring mupdf@1.28.0, a bundled production AGPL package, because the pruned lockfile marked it dev), X-1 (the audit report's INSTRUMENT column was scoped to scripts/ while a filesystem probe landed under packages/kernel/src — W-1's blind spot recurring by root rather than by pattern), X-2 (that probe's own case-folding guard read the whole path instead of the basename, so it was measuring whether the DIRECTORY name folds; found by writing its first test), X-3 (proof:documenthandlers took its control PDF from a gitignored directory another step writes — present locally, absent on a runner, skipped on 13 runs and failed the first time it ran) and X-4 (proof:hookprobe asserted check:docs' global exit code, so it went red for an unrelated gate). All six closed; and 81b9b2b..9303bb5 — the Node floor job, the error reporter and the publish decision, a range made almost entirely of instruments — findings Y-1 (four proofs print a fixed roster of `ok` lines and a hand-written total that no executed case has to justify; measured by deleting a check and watching its `ok` line still print, exit 0 — and preCommit.proof.mjs fixed exactly this for itself inside the same range, leaving four siblings), Y-2 (the pre-commit gate measures watermark..HEAD, where HEAD is the parent, so the commit that crosses one batch is invisible to it by construction and the board goes red one push later; specified as commits + 1 and files unioned with the staged list, with a bidirectional control and a check that it cannot block the audit-recording commit), Y-3 (the reporter closed sixteen top-level handlers by enumeration and nothing stops the seventeenth — a claim with an unstated expiry, whose guard would be search-shaped and needs a positive control) and Y-4 (9303bb5 called its own guarantee unproven; re-adding the removed check fails typecheck with TS2304, so it is enforced mechanically — the commit message understated it); and 9303bb5..8519e64 — the roster, the audit gate, the quarantine sweep and the lockfile trigger, a range made almost entirely of the fixes that closed the previous one — findings Z-1 (the audit report's own classifier drops every rename state, so a proof moved AND edited lands in no column; measured at R100 and R090, and the identical field-alignment bug was fixed in the OTHER instrument inside this same range), Z-2 (the pre-commit gate takes recordsAudit from the index and the RANGE from the working tree, so an unstaged watermark edit passes the gate with nothing staged at all; measured live, EXIT=0), Z-3 (the lockfile guard's header still states the trigger this range removed, as a compound claim whose surviving clause vouches for the dead one — item 7's shape, created one commit after its detection signal was written into CLAUDE.md) and Z-4 (the roster makes a deleted case silent rather than false, and nothing anywhere pins how many cases a proof must run). All four since closed — Z-3 in 7347699, Z-1 in 93cd471 by moving the parser into gitScope.mjs, Z-2 in 98c31b1 with its own hole closed in 7fbc7e4, Z-4 in 418bcea; and 8519e64..418bcea — the four Z closures plus the Windows EPERM that took Guards down at 93cd471, the first defect in this stretch found by CI rather than by an audit — findings AA-1 (the instrument column filters ADDED FILES, so the three instruments this range added inside existing modules appeared in no column at all; the fourth axis of one classifier after pattern (W-1), root (X-1) and state (Z-1), each fix correct and each leaving the next standing), AA-2 (passRoster's contract paragraph still says there is no second thing to keep in step, thirty lines above the section that added one — item 7's fourth occurrence, fail-closed) and AA-3 (the spawn guard's Set is keyed on a case-sensitive resolved path on a case-insensitive filesystem; no live defect because both sides derive from one computation, which is a property of the callers rather than of the guard — the X-2 shape); AA-2 since closed in 6827c1d, AA-1's granularity half and AA-3 still open; and 418bcea..6827c1d — Electron landing, the Guards red it caused, the npm resolution defect underneath it, the doctrine pair and the honest-output split — findings BB-1 (advisoryRegister.proof.mjs hand-writes the roster passRoster.mjs owns, including a second copy of the skipped channel added in this very range, and declares no case count; its total is invariant at 29 across both worlds, so the fix is one line and was left undone one commit after two siblings got it), BB-2 (engineAdvisories.mjs's 'what this still does not do' documents the limit this range removed — item 7's sixth occurrence and the sharpest, because the surviving clause is SCOPE-true of the function while the two beside it are false, and the wrong belief it produces is 'build a second mechanism'), BB-3 (CLAUDE.md calls the instrument column 'new scripts', stale after both X-1's root widening and AA-1's added-files-only disclosure — the digest that tells an auditor where to look has tracked none of that column's four fixes), BB-4 (the npm_execpath harness fix has no control: measured, 22/22 still green with it reverted, because the defect was what the test INHERITED and assertions look at outputs) and BB-5 (T-1's no-derivation branch asserts two independent presences rather than that the misspelt symbol IS the unverifiable one, and UNVERIFIABLE appears in that world regardless of the mutation). All five since closed — BB-4 in e4e2e3c, BB-2 in 6d87877, BB-1 in 2a34b26, BB-3 and BB-5 in 708c414. Also recorded: the board waiter failed twice in one day and both times printed the reassuring answer, was rebuilt with an in-loop positive control, and was TRACKED NOWHERE — given a repo slot with a network-free proof in 79b368f; and 6827c1d..598b50e — the five BB closures, the board instrument, item 4b's sixth axis, and the FIRST RENDERER-SIDE CODE in this repository — findings CC-1 (the board instrument decided greenness by substring-matching its own rendered summary, so a CANCELLED run beside a successful one read GREEN: measured on the real strings, and 9292d1f — the cancelled run this module was written after — is exactly that shape; two defects in one, since the judgement also lived in the fetch shell that has no proof, and a split leaving logic on the untested side has not been made; closed in 598b50e by deriving greenness from the data in the proven module), CC-2 (channels.ts says a channel is added only when a real handler exists and calls a declared channel with nothing behind it a call that hangs; that has been false for app.info since it was declared — its only implementations are test fixtures and contract.proof.mjs, and no ContractHandlers map is registered with ipcMain at all) and CC-3 (CLAUDE.md's item-1 example describes MONSTERA_GITLEAKS in the past tense as an override that was removed; it is live at gitleaks.mjs:464 — but the mechanism is sound, both callers run the canary immediately, verified rather than taken from the comment, so this is a documentation mismatch in the checklist an auditor reads, not an open door). CC-1 closed, CC-2 and CC-3 open. Y-1 verified fully closed: all 32 total-printing proofs derive their number. THE RANGE THAT CHANGED WHAT THE RANGES ARE FOR — the audit's input had become its own output, seven Stage 0 rows are renderer-side and all seven read '—', and the CSP invariant is deferred because no renderer exists to read it from; next is the skeleton, not the queue; and 598b50e..90d9b6e — ALL FOUR CONTRACT SURFACES, packages/ui stopping being `export {}`, and Electron provisioned against a recorded pin — findings DD-1 (the pin is a RECORD, not an ENFORCEMENT: node_modules/electron/index.js ends with module.exports = getElectronPath(), which calls downloadElectron() when the binary is absent, so --ignore-scripts DEFERS the electron_use_remote_checksums hatch to first require() rather than closing it; nothing consumes the pinned binary — git grep finds no caller outside its own proof — and require('electron') resolves to node_modules/electron/dist rather than .tools/. The naive fix is a TRAP: an .npmrc carrying ignore-scripts=true also disables this repository's own prepare script, which installs the git hooks, silently disarming the secret scan and the escape-guard. The remedy is ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH, read before both downloadElectron call sites, which makes the download path UNREACHABLE rather than discouraged — plus a guard that fails when node_modules/electron/dist exists; with one measured wrinkle, that index.js:31 joins the override with executablePath || 'electron' read from an absent path.txt, so it names a file with no .exe on Windows) and DD-2 (a process finding: a design question already settled in docs/JOURNAL.md at 132c2e7 was brought as an open one, and a correction was filed stating no Electron pin existed — which would have put TWO ENTRIES DISAGREEING ABOUT ONE AUTHORITY into the record, B3a inside the journal eleven commits after B3a became law. Two separable failures: the digest search was scoped Grep(path:'scripts') and never looked at docs/, which is X-1's root axis again; and `git grep -il` then RETURNED the right file and its filename list was read as the answer — not 4b's shape, because the search worked and no positive control catches a reader stopping early). Both open. Also corrected inside the range: 'two independent sources agreeing byte for byte' overstated the checksum cross-check — the release SHASUMS256.txt and the package's checksums.json are TWO CHANNELS FROM ONE PUBLISHER, which defeats a compromise of one distribution path and is not two attestations. The watermark never equals HEAD at recording time — see scripts/lib/auditWatermark.mjs; and 90d9b6e..d4c01c1 — a range made almost entirely of instruments, audited BEFORE the window unit so that instruments and the first feature code would not share one range — findings FF-1 (a shared list with two consumers had a proof on one of them: PLAIN_NODE_EXTENSIONS widens the lint glob and the runtime scan together, only the scan had a case, and the fact that hid it — no .js or .cjs exists under scripts/ today — is the fact that will change) and FF-2 (ESLint does not expand a SINGLE-element brace, so `scripts/**` + `/*.{mjs}` matched nothing while `/*.mjs` matched everything; invisible with three extensions, and it fails as 103 `not found by the project service` parsing errors that name tsconfig rather than the glob — a failure impossible to miss and impossible to attribute). Both closed in d4c01c1, FF-2 by making the length-one case unrepresentable as an array rather than checking for it, and by putting the attribution into the new case's own diagnostic. Nine reviewer findings EE-1..EE-10 all raised and closed inside the range, including EE-7, a process finding in which two documents' over-generalised 'ESLint does not reach scripts/' — false; it globs every .mjs with one rule enabled — produced a wrong B4-sized ruling for work that was three lines. ITEM 2a PAID IN ITS CORRECTED FORM: the electron-import coverage did not move from two workflows to one (it was in guards.yml only, then ci.yml only, both two-platform); it moved from a job that could ALWAYS look to one that can only look after `npm ci` succeeds, and both halves — ESLint's static and the scan's runtime — now share that single dependency, with the 138-commit precedent as the reason that is not theoretical. AA-1's granularity half open for a THIRD consecutive range and again the axis that hid something: three instruments arrived as functions inside an existing module and appeared in no column, and both findings came from reading modified-proof diffs. The net-diff caveat earned its keep — electron.proof.mjs reads +8 -0 while its roster went 8 -> 11 -> 8 inside the range, so a rule check was added and removed and the net shows neither; and d4c01c1..a66e1e6 — Electron provisioned in CI and THE SHELL STARTS: a hardened BrowserWindow, both permission handlers, the sender check, a launcher naming the pinned binary through electronBinaryPath(), and on windows-latest the FIRST security property this repository has verified against a running Chromium rather than against the source that configures it (the CSP read from the response as received, and the renderer observed refusing a connect-src fetch and an eval). RECORDED WHILE MAIN IS RED, deliberately, because the gate counts commits+1 and the pending Linux fix waits behind this entry — findings GG-1 (a commit added a file under scripts/ and did not run the proof that scans scripts/, G-1's shape; rule: when a commit adds a file to a directory some proof scans, that proof is in the pre-commit set whatever the change is about), GG-2 ('only the read-back step fails' was ASSERTED and was the premise under four hypotheses about a step that had not run — step CONCLUSIONS and DURATIONS are on the public API, only raw logs are behind the 403, and the one-second duration eliminated every hang hypothesis at once), GG-3 (the harness could only fail by hanging, FF-2's shape — and the commit that fixed it is itself a finding: correct fixes written against an unconfirmed symptom, the banned reflex with good engineering attached), GG-4 (THREE second opinions in one module, all B3a, all found by running it: the direct-invocation guard that exited 0 provisioning nothing on Windows, tmpdir staging that rename could not leave across volumes, and an extractor comment true on macOS and false on Linux while the list was used on both), GG-5 (the CSP enforcement probe was a fixture the defect handles correctly — a fetch to a bogus host fails on DNS whatever the policy says, so it reported 'blocked' for a request CSP had just been loosened to permit, and survived the exact mutation it existed to catch; now read from securitypolicyviolation, which only CSP raises) and GG-6 (nothing established the published binary could be EXECUTED — the available:true shape, raised by the reviewing seat, fixed in the commit this entry unblocks). Item 2a: the read-back is a strengthening where provisioned and a new 'could not look' elsewhere, printing UNVERIFIABLE rather than 'nothing to check'. Open: AA-1, AA-3, CC-3, DD-2, BB-6, Y-3, and the MuPDF cache's restore-without-reverify, which is not the same shape because it caches a built tree with no pin to check against; and a66e1e6..03fcf9b — the CSP becoming law as invariant 27 with this document as its writer of record, and the §2 read-back widening from one item to five, owed on the FILE threshold at 24 of 24 rather than on commits — findings HH-1 (the preload had NEVER EXECUTED: tsc emits ESM into a "type": "module" package and a sandboxed preload is loaded as CommonJS, announced through Electron's preload-error event and through nothing else — no stderr, no exception, a window that came up looking correct; proof:preload and proof:contract both passed CORRECTLY about a file nothing had run, because the defect is not in the file. Closed in-range by bundling to CJS through a new @monstera/contract/bridge leaf: 137,809 bytes through the package root, 233 through the leaf, since channelIds = Object.keys(channels) is a top-level evaluation nothing prunes around), HH-2 (the range's own new navigation probe was VACUOUS and only the mutation step found it — https://example.org/ produces zero loads when the guard refuses it and zero when the machine has no network, so it could not tell a working guard from an offline runner; item 4's fixture rule in the same file that already records being bitten by it on example.invalid four commits earlier, in a comment that was on screen while the probe was written beneath it. Now the loaded document plus a query string: on disk so it loads with no network, different href so the guard refuses it), HH-3 (ADR-0020 offered two independently-sufficient reasons and had executed one; the resolution claim was documentation written as evidence, measured afterwards as `Error: module not found: @monstera/contract/bridge` from a CJS preload — the claim is true, its status was not, and the ADR carries a dated correction rather than a silent upgrade), HH-4 (the UNVERIFIABLE block hand-writes `9 case(s)` and nine lines beside a roster declared 13/4, so the mechanism whose whole job is to not overstate carries a literal that goes stale the moment a runtime case is added — B3a inside the honesty mechanism), HH-5 (window.ts's HERE comment still says the sibling `preload.js`, eight lines above the comment written IN THE SAME COMMIT explaining why it is preload.cjs — item 7's compound claim, ninth occurrence and the second created BY the fix, with the surviving clause vouching for the dead one) and HH-6 (proof:rendererpolicy resolves the harness, the declared policy and the preload from dist/ and nothing detects a STALE dist; proof:testresolution exists for exactly this class on the test side, and staleness is the one failure CLAUDE.md names as unreachable by a positive control). HH-1, HH-2 and HH-3 closed; HH-4, HH-5 and HH-6 open. Item 2a: the pin agreement is a strengthening with NO provisioning condition — two strings, every machine — while the UNVERIFIABLE block grew 3 lines to 9, which reads as a blind spot tripling and is not one: the intent half runs everywhere and gained an assertion, and what is newly unverifiable is enforcement that was previously verified nowhere. Also recorded: style-src 'unsafe-inline' was DROPPED rather than pinned, outside the ruling that ordered the amendment and flagged as such; and GG-8's convert-on-touch trigger has NOT fired — two workflow steps were edited and neither touches the Electron tree
